comment: The table of the typed family of the tests and of the one judgement of the closed-world
tests: the three tables of test/fort/support/generator.ft and the judgement of
test/fort/support/judgement.ft. The first 6 rows each take one row out of TYPES, STORAGES
or OPERATIONS: a type with no text is no type, a storage class with no place is no storage
class, and an operation with no text is no operation, so the mutant compiles and the family
loses the cells or the statements of that row. Two rows stand for each table, the first
row and another one. test/fort/owner/typed/count_test.ft prints the count of the cells,
the vocabulary size of each cell, the count of the cells of each operation and the count
of the functions of 0 to 3 operations; a row is caught when a line changes.
Each row `judgement-*` changes one rule of the judgement: which verdicts it judges, what
the disposition table of test/fort/support/disposition.ft decides, which events are errors
and which report line takes an event, the function and the line that a report line names,
the bare `del` that a line at a `cast` names, the path that names the entry module, the
`dead` markers of an abort, the release-only bit of a drop, the verdict `reported`, the
inputs of a run, the end of a run, each kind of error of a failure, the class of a failure
and of an item of the gate, the statements that vacate a place and the events that end its
vacated state, the statements that vacate an inner owner of a place, the statements
between a statement that vacates and the store that fills, the list KNOWN and the exit
status. test/fort/owner/typed/judgement_test.ft prints each of those rules over tables and
over a batch of functions that it writes. The 2 rows `judgement-part-*` change the main
function of a part, which the judgement test does not call: the second stage runs part 6
of the family, the part with the fewest failures. The other 7 parts run in no stage.
test/fort/owner/oracle_test.ft takes each ruling from the same module, and
tools/mutations/disposition.json holds the rows that the oracle test must catch.
The sources are support modules of the tests, so the build only joins them into
build/typed_support.txt, and the md5 guard reads that file. The table runs in the Linux VM
with the debug preset after `tools/vm build`.
